Arabic root r-b-ʿ; rub (quarter), rubai (quatrain) and murabba (square) come from the same root.
Latin Roma; from romanice "in the Roman tongue" derive roman, romantik and romans.
Old Turkic ötkün- "to narrate, to imitate"; öykünmek and the Language Reform (1930s) coinage öykü come from the same root.
Old Turkic teŋe- "to measure, to try"; denemek, deneme, deney and deneyim derive from the same root.
Old Turkic tiz- "to string, to line up"; dizmek, dize, dizi and dizin come from the same root.
Arabic root q-ṭ-ʿ; kıta (piece), kat'i (definite), inkıta and maktu derive from the same root.
Old Turkic bet "face"; betim (Language Reform, 1930s) and betimlemek derive from the same root.
The Arabic root ş-b-h; teşbih (simile), müşabih and şüphe (doubt born of resemblance) with its derivatives şüpheli, şüphesiz and şüpheci come from the same root.
Arabic root c-w-z; mecaz (passage, transfer), caiz (permissible), cevaz and icazet derive from the same root.
Arabic root c-n-s (from Greek génos); cins, cinsiyet and cinas (wordplay on words of the same kind) come from the same root.
Old Turkic oyun/oyna-; oyun, oynamak, oyuncu and oyuncak derive from the same root.

column2: to resemble, to serve as an example
column3: Arabic root m-ṯ-l; misal, mesel, temsil, timsal and mümessil come from the same root.
Arabic root n-q-d; nakit (sorted, ready money), tenkit and münekkit derive from the same root.
Old Turkic elge- "to sift"; eleştirmek and eleştiri (Language Reform, 1930s) come from the same root.
Ancient Greek krínein "to separate"; kritik, kriter, kriz (moment of decision) and endokrin (secreting inward) derive from the same root.
Ancient Greek týpos "blow, stamp"; tip, tipik and tipo come from the same root.
Arabic root ʾ-l-f; müellif (compiler, author), telif and ülfet derive from the same root.
Arabic root ʾ-ṯ-r; eser (trace), tesir and müessir come from the same root. Asır and asri form a separate family from the root ʿ-ṣ-r "age".
Arabic root ṣ-r-f; sarf, masraf and tasarruf derive from the same root.
Ancient Greek sophós "wise"; felsefe (via Arabic), filozof, feylesof, sofist and sofistike come from the same root.
Arabic root n-ṭ-q; mantık, nutuk and natıka derive from the same root.
Old Anatolian Turkish kavra- "to grasp"; kavramak, kavram and kavrayış come from the same root.
Arabic root f-h-m; fehim, mefhum and tefhim derive from the same root.
Arabic root m-d-d; madde, müddet, imdat and temdit come from the same root.
Arabic root ʿ-n-y; mana and manevi derive from the same root.
Old Turkic kirtü "true"; gerçek and gerçeklik come from the same root.
Arabic root c-h-l; cahil, cehalet and meçhul derive from the same root.
Old Turkic kuşku; kuşku and kuşkulanmak come from the same root.
ınan- "to trust" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; inanmak, inanç and inak (dogma) derive from the same root.
Arabic root f-ḏ-l; fazilet, fazıl, fazla and fuzuli come from the same root.
Arabic root r-w-d; irade and murat derive from the same root.
Old Turkic iste- "to seek, to want"; istemek, istek and istenç come from the same root.
öz "self" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; özgür, özne, özel, özet and özgün were coined from the same root during the Language Reform (1930s).
Arabic root ṣ-w-f; sof (wool), sufi (wearer of wool) and tasavvuf come from the same root.
Arabic root w-ḥ-d; vahit, vahdet, tevhit and ittihat derive from the same root.
Arabic root b-q-y; beka, baki and bakiye come from the same root.
Arabic root q-y-s; kıyas and mikyas derive from the same root.
öŋ "front" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; önce, öncü, önem, öneri and önerme come from the same root.
Ancient Greek légein "to say"; diyalektik and leksikon derive from the same root; it is related to the logos family.
Ancient Greek êthos "custom"; etik and etos come from the same root.
Ancient Greek idéa "form, appearance"; ide, idea, ideal, idealizm, ideoloji and idol derive from the same root.
Latin mater "mother"; via materia (mother substance), materyal, materyalizm and matris come from the same root.
Latin ratio "reckoning, reason"; rasyonel, rasyonalizm and rasyon derive from the same root.
Old Anatolian Turkish sez- "to sense"; sezmek and sezgi come from the same root.
belle- "to learn", related to Old Turkic belgü "sign"; bellemek, bellek and belleten derive from the same root.
Arabic root ḫ-ṭ-r; hatır (mind, heart) and hatıra come from the same root.
Old Turkic us "mind"; uslu and usçuluk derive from the same root.
törü "law" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; töre, türe, türemek, türev and tür come from the same root.
Arabic root m-t-ʿ; metâ (goods enjoyed), emtia (commodities) and temettü (dividend) derive from the same root.
Arabic root k-s-b; kesp (earnings), kâsıp (earner), iktisap (acquisition), müktesep and müktesebat come from the same root.
Arabic root r-b-ḥ; ribh (profit), rabıh (profitable) and murabaha (sale at a profit) derive from the same root.
Arabic root r-h-n; rehin, merhun (pledged), mürtehin (pledgee) and rehine (hostage) come from the same root.
Arabic root ş-r-y; şira, iştira (purchase) and muştarī (buyer) > müşteri come from the same root. Şirket and müşterek form a separate family from the root ş-r-k "to be a partner".
Arabic root c-b-y; cibayet (tax collection) and cabi (tax collector) derive from the same root.
Arabic root q-r-ḍ; karz (loan), ikraz (lending), istikraz (borrowing), mukriz and karzen come from the same root.
Arabic root r-b-w; riba (interest, usury), ribacı, together with mürebbi and mürebbiye (one who rears and educates), derive from the same root.
Arabic root f-y-ḍ; faiz (that which accrues, overflows), faizli, faizci, feyiz (overflowing abundance) and feyezan (flood) derive from the same root.
Arabic root m-w-l; mal, maliye, mali, maliyet, emval (goods), temvil and mütemevvil (wealthy) derive from the same root.

column2: to cross; to learn a lesson; to reckon
column3: Arabic root ʿ-b-r; itibar, itibari (nominal), ibret (a lesson drawn from the past) and muteber (deemed valid) come from the same root.
Arabic root d-w-l; devlet (power that changes hands), düvel, tedavül (circulation from hand to hand), mütedavil and devletçi derive from the same root.
Arabic root ṣ-f-w; saf, safi (unadulterated), tasfiye (purification; liquidation), tasfiyeci and musaffa come from the same root.
Arabic root q-ṣ-ṣ; kısas (retaliation), takas (settling accounts, barter) and kıssa (an event followed; a tale) derive from the same root.
Arabic root ḍ-m-n; tazmin (compensating for a loss), zımni (implicit), zımnen and mutazammın derive from the same root.
Arabic root r-w-c; revaç (demand, currency), rayiç (current price) and tervic (promoting the sale of) derive from the same root.
Arabic root r-ġ-b; rağbet (demand, desire), rağbetli and mergup (desired) come from the same root.
Arabic root d-ḫ-l; dahil, dahili, ithal (bringing in), ithalat, ithalatçı, müdahale and medhal (entrance) derive from the same root.
Arabic root k-l-f; mükellef (obligated), mükellefiyet, teklif, külfet, tekellüf and tekâlif (taxes) derive from the same root.
Arabic root ṯ-n-y; istisna (exception), istisnai and müstesna derive from the same root.
Arabic root r-f-h; refah (prosperity), müreffeh and terfih derive from the same root.
Arabic root y-w-m; yevmiye (daily wage) and eyyam (days) derive from the same root.
Arabic root q-s-ṭ; kıst (share), taksit (division into installments) and taksitli come from the same root.
Arabic root ṣ-ġ-r; sagir (small), asgari (minimum) and tasgir (diminution) derive from the same root.
Arabic root ʾ-h-l; ehil (competent for a task), ehli (domesticated) and ehliyet derive from the same root.
Arabic root m-h-r; mahir (skilled) and maharet (skill) come from the same root.
Arabic root d-r-k; idrak (comprehension), müdrik, tedarik (procuring in time) and tedarikçi come from the same root.
Arabic quadriliteral root s-m-s-r; simsar (broker), simsariye (brokerage fee) and simsarlık derive from the same root.
Arabic root t-ḥ-f; tuhaf (rare, strange), tuhafiye (pleasant small wares) and tuhafiyeci derive from the same root.
Arabic root b-z-z; bez, bezzaz (cloth merchant), bezzaziye and, with the Persian suffix -istan, bedesten come from the same root.
Arabic root d-b-ġ; debbağ (tanner), dibagat and tabakhane derive from the same root.
Arabic root s-r-c; saraç (saddler), saraçlık and siraç (lamp) come from the same root.
Arabic root b-q-l; bakla, bakkal (greengrocer), bakkaliye, bakkallık and bakliyat come from the same root.
Arabic root ʿ-ṭ-r; ıtır (scent), ıtriyat, attar and aktar (seller of scents and spices) derive from the same root.
Arabic root c-l-d; cilt, ciltçi, mücellit (bookbinder) and teclit (bookbinding) derive from the same root.
The root c-w-h-r, which passed into Arabic from Persian gōhar; cevher, cevahir, mücevher and mücevherat derive from the same root.
Arabic root w-r-q; varak (leaf), varaka (document) and evrak (papers) derive from the same root.
Arabic root b-l-ġ; meblağ (the amount reached), bâliğ, tebliğ (conveying), belagat and mübalağa come from the same root.
Persian bāzār "market, bazaar"; pazar, pazarlık, pazarlama, pazarlamacı, pazarbaşı and, from bāzārgān, bezirgân derive from the same root.
Persian ḫudā "owner, master"; kethüda (kad-ḫudā: master of the house) and kethüdalık carry this element; kâhya is the popular form of the same word.
Persian dast "hand"; dest, destek (dastak: support), destekli and destur (giving a hand, permission) come from the same root.
Persian sipurden "to entrust"; sipariş and siparişçi derive from this verb.
Persian parākande "dispersed"; perakende (piecemeal sale, retail), perakendeci and perakendecilik come from the same word.
Persian kār "work; gain"; kâr, kârlı, kârsız, kârlılık, kârhane (workshop) and kârgir derive from the same root.
Persian bahā "value"; paha, pahalı, pahasız, pahalanmak and pahalılaşmak come from the same root.
Old Turkic kedük/gedik "breach"; gedik (a gap in a wall; a guild monopoly right) and gedikli come from the same root.
Old Anatolian Turkish ısmarla- "to entrust, to order"; ısmarlamak and ısmarlama derive from the same root.
Old Turkic kuy- "to pour liquid or cast metal"; kuyum, kuyumcu and kuyumculuk derive from the same root.
Old Turkic uçuz "worthless, easy"; ucuz, ucuzluk, ucuzlamak and ucuzlatmak derive from the same root.
Old Turkic ur- "to strike" (with a prothetic v-); vurmak, vurgun (ill-gotten gain), vurguncu and vurgunculuk come from the same root.
Old Turkic kazġan- "to gain"; kazanmak, kazanç, kazançlı and kazanım derive from the same root.
tamga "seal, mark" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; damga, tamga, damgalamak and damgalı come from the same root; it also passed into Mongolian and Russian.
Old Turkic teŋ "equal"; denk, denge, dengeli, denklik and denkleştirmek derive from the same root.
Old Turkic tüke- "to come to an end"; tükenmek, tüketmek, tüketim, tüketici and tükenmez come from the same root.
Old Turkic tagıl- "to scatter"; dağılmak, dağıtmak, dağıtım and dağıtıcı derive from the same root.
kamuġ "all, whole" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; kamu (the public), kamulaştırma and kamulaştırmak come from the same root.
Old Turkic ser- "to spread out"; sermek, sergi, sergileme and sergici derive from the same root.
Old Turkic tek "alone"; tek, tekel (single hand, monopoly), tekelci and tekelcilik come from the same root.
From the Sogdian word pwrc "debt"; borç, borçlu, borçlanmak, borçlanma and borçsuz come from the same root.
Latin grossus "thick"; via German Groschen (a large coin), kuruş and kuruşluk derive from the same root.
Ancient Greek drakhmḗ "handful; unit of currency"; via Arabic dirham, dirhem, and Greek drahmi come from the same root.
Latin libra "scales, unit of weight"; Italian lira, liret and, via French livre, libre derive from the same root.
Italian banca "money-changer's bench" (Germanic bank "bench"); banka, banker, bankacı, bankacılık, banko and banknot come from the same root.
Ancient Greek Eurṓpē "Europe"; avro and euro, the names of the European currency, are clipped from this name.
Latin credere "to trust"; kredi (trust, credit), kredili, kreditör, kredibilite and akreditif come from the same root.
Latin primus "first"; prim (first reward), primli and primitif derive from the same root.
Latin bilanx "having two pans"; via Italian bilancio, bilanço, and via French balance, balans derive from the same root.
Latin liquere "to flow"; likit, likidite (convertibility into cash) and likidasyon come from the same root.
Ancient Greek stíba "heap"; istif, istifçi, istifçilik and istiflemek come from the same root.
Latin merx "merchandise"; from commercium, via Greek kommérkion, come gümrük, gümrükçü, gümrüklü and gümrükleme, together with market, hipermarket and merkantilizm, all from the same root.
Latin flare "to blow"; enflasyon (swelling), deflasyon and stagflasyon come from the same root.
Latin valere "to be strong, to be worth"; valör, devalüasyon and revalüasyon derive from the same root.
Latin pater "father"; patron (protective father), patronluk and patronaj come from the same root.
Ancient Greek díkē "right"; from sýndikos derive sendika, sendikacı and sendikal.
Latin secare "to cut"; sektör (a cut, section), sektörel and seksiyon come from the same root.
Latin margo "edge"; marj (margin) and marjinal derive from the same root.
Latin liber "free"; liberal, liberalizm and liberalleşme come from the same root.

column3: Latin legere "to gather"; kolektif, kolektivizm, koleksiyon and, via legio "a gathered body of troops", lejyon come from the same root.
French bloc "mass" (Dutch blok); blok, blokaj and bloke derive from the same root.

Latin charta "paper" (Greek khártēs); kart, kartel (written agreement) and kartela come from the same root.

Latin fundus "bottom"; fon (a source of money) and fonlamak come from the same root.
Latin experiri "to try"; eksper (tried, expert) and ekspertiz come from the same root.
Latin securus "safe"; via Italian sicurtà, sigorta, sigortacı, sigortalamak and reasürans derive from the same root.
Arabic naʿl "shoe, horseshoe"; nal, nalbant (one who fits horseshoes) and nalbur (one who cuts horseshoes; hardware dealer), nalburiye come from the same root.
Old Turkic bıç- "to cut"; biçki (cutting cloth), bıçkı (large saw) and bıçak derive from the same root.
Old Turkic ked- "to wear" > giy-; giyecek, giydirmek, giyinik and giyimli are derivatives of this root.
Old Turkic egir- "to twist on a spindle"; the verb eğirmek and iğ (spindle) share the same root.
Old Turkic bük- "to bend, to twist"; büküm and bükülü derive from this root.
Old Turkic kırk- "to shear wool"; kırkmak and kırkım (shearing season) share the same root.
Old Turkic kak- "to strike, to hammer"; kakmak, kakma (metal inlay) and kakmacı form the same family.
Old Turkic kabar- "to swell"; kabartma, kabartmak and kabarık derive from this root.
Old Turkic bile- "to sharpen a knife"; bilemek, bileği (whetstone), bileme and bileyici share the same root.
Old Turkic tın- "to make a sound, to breathe"; tını, tınlamak and tıngırdatmak come from this root.
The onomatopoeic root çıŋ; çınlamak and çınlama describe a metallic sound.
Old Turkic yüz- "to move through water"; yüzmek, yüzme, yüzücü and yüzücülük derive from this root.
Old Turkic tal- "to dive, to sink"; dalmak, dalgıç and dalış share the same root.
Old Turkic tep- "to kick"; tepmek, tekme (tep-me) and tekmelemek come from this root.
Old Turkic yum- "to close, to ball up"; yumak and yumruklamak (yumruk) share the same root.
Old Turkic bur- "to twist, to turn"; burmak, burgu and burma (a twisted bracelet) derive from this root.
Old Turkic tel- "to pierce"; delgi and delgeç were coined from this root during the Language Reform (1930s).
Old Turkic töşe- "to spread"; döşemek, döşemeci, döşemecilik and döşekçi come from this root.
Old Turkic toğra- "to chop"; doğramacı and doğramacılık name the craft of woodworking.
Old Turkic egek "file"; eğe and eğelemek share the same root.
Old Turkic yırt- "to tear"; yırtmak and yırtmaç (a slit in a skirt) share the same root.

column2: to pass through flame, to iron
column3: Old Turkic üt- "to singe in flame"; ütü, ütülemek and ütücü share the same root.
Arabic root z-y-n; ziynet (ornament), tezyin (decoration), tezyinat and müzeyyen (adorned) share the same root.
Arabic root l-b-s "to wear"; libas (garment) and melbusat (clothing) derive from this root.
Arabic root n-s-c "to weave"; nesic (tissue), mensucat (textiles) and nessac (weaver) form the same family.
Arabic root d-b-ġ "to tan"; debbağ, debbağhane, dibagat, tabaklamak and tabakçı share the same root.
Arabic root ṭ-b-l; tabla, tablakâr and davulcu (ṭabl "drum") share the same root.
Arabic root s-b-q "to get ahead"; müsabaka (competition) and müsabık (competitor) come from this root.
Arabic root r-q-ṣ; rakkas (dancer, pendulum) and raksetmek come from the same root.
Arabic root n-ġ-m; naġma (melody) > nağme comes from this root. Muganni and teganni form a separate family from the root ġ-n-y "to sing".
Arabic root ḫ-t-m; hatem (signet ring) and hitam (end) come from this root.
Arabic root d-l-k "to rub"; tellak (bath attendant who scrubs) and tellaklık come from this root.
Persian dūḫtan/dūz- "to sew" and darzī "tailor" from the same root; çuvaldız (sack-sewing needle) and terzilik belong to this family.
Persian tarāşīdan "to carve"; tıraş and talaş (shavings) come from this root.
The Persian suffix -dān "container"; çaydanlık, yağdan and sürmedan are formed with this suffix.
French chiffe "rag"; şifon (a thin fabric) and şifonyer (a linen chest) derive from the same word.
Latin cannabis "hemp"; kanaviçe and kanava take their names from hemp cloth.
Latin tornare "to turn on a lathe"; torna, tornacı, tornacılık, tornalamak and turnuva share the same root.
Latin recordari "to remember"; rekor and rekortmen reached Turkish through English record.
Ancient Greek âthlon "contest"; atletizm, dekatlon and triatlon come from this root.
The Ancient Greek place name Marathṓn; maraton and maratoncu derive from this name.
Ancient Greek ákros "topmost, highest"; akrobat (one who walks on tiptoe) and akrobasi share the same root.
Ancient Greek chorós "dance, dancing troupe"; horon, koreografi and koreograf come from this root.
Late Latin ballare "to dance"; balo and balerin passed into Turkish through Italian.
Latin campus "field"; şampiyon (campio "fighter in the field"), şampiyona and şampiyonluk share the same root.
aş "food" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; aşçı, aşevi and sütlaç (milk dish) come from the same root.
Old Turkic toŋ- "to freeze"; donmak and dondurma derive from the same root.
Arabic root ṭ-b-ḫ; mutfak (maṭbaḫ: cooking place) and tabhane come from the same root.
Arabic root ḏ-y-f; ziyafet (entertaining guests) and dayf (guest) come from the same root; in Turkish only ziyafet survives from this root.
Arabic root ḥ-l-w; helva, helvacı and halavet (sweetness) come from the same root.
Latin sal "salt"; salça, sos, salata (salted), salam and salamura derive from the same root.
Arabic root ḫ-m-r; hamur (fermented), mahmur and humar (hangover) come from the same root.
Latin coquere "to cook"; bisküvi (twice-baked) comes from the same root.
Late Latin pasta "dough"; pasta, pastane, pastacı and pastel (paste paint) derive from the same root.
The word kuş, attested in the Orkhon Inscriptions; baykuş, kuşluk, kuşbaşı, yağmurkuşu, ishakkuşu, kuşburnu, kuşkonmaz, kuşbakışı, kuşçu, kızkuşu and ardıçkuşu come from the same root.
Old Turkic sag- "to milk"; sağmak, sağım and sağmal (milking animal) derive from the same root.
Turkish yavru "young of an animal"; yavrulamak, yavrucak and yavruağzı (a color) come from the same root.
Old Turkic müŋüz, later boynuz; boynuzlamak, boynuzlu, boynuzsuz and tekboynuz derive from the same root.
Old Turkic kudruk "tail"; kuyruklu, kuyruksuz, kuyrukkakan (a bird), atkuyruğu and tilkikuyruğu (plants) come from the same root.
Old Turkic tü "hair, feather"; tüylü, tüysüz, tüylenmek, tüyleme and kuştüyü derive from the same root.
kanat in the Dîvânu Lugâti't-Türk; kanatlı, kanatsız, kanatlanmak, kanatçık and kınkanatlı come from the same root.
Old Turkic yapurgak "leaf"; yaprakçık, yapraklı and yapraklanmak derive from the same root.
Old Turkic yılan; yılanbalığı, yılanyastığı (a plant) and yılancık (a skin disease) come from the same root.
Turkish böcek; böcü, böcekçil, ipekböceği, ateşböceği, uğurböceği, hamamböceği, cırcırböceği, ağustosböceği, mayısböceği, geyikböceği and sümüklüböcek derive from the same root.
Old Turkic ısır- "to bite"; ısırgan (the stinging plant) and ısırık come from the same root.
Old Turkic sok- "to insert, to thrust"; sokmak (to sting), sokulmak and sokulgan derive from the same root.

column2: to wear away with the teeth
column3: Turkish kemir-; kemirmek, kemirgen (gnawing animal, rodent) and kemirme come from the same root.
Old Turkic öt- "to sing (of birds)"; ötmek, ötücü, ötüş, ötüşmek and ötleğen (a bird) come from the same root.
tüne-, related to Old Turkic tün "night"; tünemek and tünek (a bird's night perch) derive from the same root.
Old Turkic küd- "to herd, to watch over"; gütmek, güdüm and güdümlü derive from the same root.
ot "plant" in the Orkhon Inscriptions; otlamak, otlatmak, otçul, otobur, otlu, isot, semizotu, çörekotu, dereotu, sinirotu and şerbetçiotu come from the same root.

Ancient Greek khrôma "color"; krom, kromozom (a body that takes color) and kromatik come from the same root.

Ancient Greek kardía "heart"; kardiyoloji, kardiyak and elektrokardiyogram come from the same root; it is an Indo-European cognate of Latin cor.
Ancient Greek neûron "sinew, nerve"; nöroloji, nöron, nevroz and nevralji derive from the same root.
Ancient Greek psykhḕ "breath, soul"; psikoloji, psikiyatri, psikolog and psişik come from the same root.
Ancient Greek haîma "blood"; hematoloji, anemi, lösemi, hemoglobin and hemoroid derive from the same root.
Ancient Greek gastḕr "belly, stomach"; gastrit, gastronomi and gastroenteroloji come from the same root.
Ancient Greek ostéon "bone"; osteoporoz and osteopati derive from the same root; it is related to Latin os.
Ancient Greek orthós "straight"; ortopedi, ortodonti, ortodoks and ortografi come from the same root.
Ancient Greek paîs "child"; pedagoji, pedagog, pediatri and ansiklopedi (all-round education) derive from the same root.
Ancient Greek thermós "hot"; termos, termal, termik and termometre come from the same root.
Arabic root q-s-w; kasvet (gloom; hardness) and kasvetli come from the same root. Kisve and kispet belong to the separate root k-s-w "to clothe".

column2: to build a dome; to be round
column3: Arabic root q-b-b; qubba (dome) > kubbe and kubbealtı come from the same root. Kebap is not from this root: kabāb is traced to an Aramaic/Akkadian root meaning "to burn, to char".

The Arabic root ʿ-ẕ-m; ʿaẕamet (greatness) > azamet, muʿaẕẕam > muazzam, and sadrazam (ṣadr-ı aʿẕam, "the greatest chief") come from the same root. Azim belongs to the separate root ʿ-z-m "to be resolute".
Arabic root k-ṯ-r; kaṯra (multitude) > kesret comes from this root. Kesir and inkisar belong to the separate root k-s-r "to break".

column2: to be short, to fall short
column3: Arabic root q-ṣ-r; quṣūr (deficiency) > kusur, kusurlu, kusursuz and taqṣīr (shortening; negligence) > taksir come from the same root. Kesir and inkisar belong to the separate root k-s-r "to break".
Arabic root r-q-b; raqīb (watcher) > rakip, rekabet (mutual watching, rivalry), murakabe and mürakıp derive from the same root. Merkep and terkip belong to the separate root r-k-b "to mount".
Arabic root ʿ-ṣ-r; ʿaṣr (age, century; late afternoon) > asır and asri (contemporary) come from the same root. Eser and tesir belong to the separate root ʾ-ṯ-r "trace".
Arabic root ẕ-r-f; ẕarīf (fine, elegant) > zarif, zarifçe and ẕarāfa > zarafet come from the same root.

Latin cor (cordis) "heart"; accordare "to bring hearts into agreement" > French accord > akor and akordeon come from the same root. Rekor (recordari, "to bring back to the heart") goes back to the same Latin root.
Old Turkic verb ört- "to cover, to conceal"; örtü (örtüg) and örtünmek come from the same root. Örmek (ör-) is a separate root.
Old Turkic verb ilet- / elt- "to carry away"; iletmek, iletken, iletim and the Language Reform coinages ileti and iletişim come from the same root. Ulaşmak (ula-) and il- are separate roots.
Arabic root f-r-ḍ; farz, farize, faraza, faraziye and mefruz come from the same root. Fert and münferit belong to the separate root f-r-d "to be single".
Arabic root ḥ-c-r; hacer (stone), hücre (small room), hacir (restriction) and mahcur derive from the same root. Hicret and muhacir belong to the separate root h-c-r "to migrate".
Arabic root ḥ-k-r; ihtikâr (profiteering) and muhtekir (profiteer) derive from the same root. Hakaret and hakir belong to the separate root ḥ-q-r.
Arabic root ḫ-y-r; hayır (goodness), hayırlı, hayrat, ihtiyar (choice; elder) and muhtar (chosen) derive from the same root. Hayret and hayran belong to the separate root ḥ-y-r.
Arabic root ḫ-z-n; hazine, hazne, mahzen (storeroom) and, via Italian magazzino, mağaza come from the same root. Hüzün and mahzun belong to the separate root ḥ-z-n.
Arabic root l-ḥ-m "flesh; to weld"; liḥām > lehim, lehimci and lehimlemek come from this root. İlham belongs to the separate root l-h-m.
Arabic root ş-q-w; şaqī (wretch; brigand) > şaki, eşkıya (its plural) and şekavet derive from the same root. Şikâyet belongs to the separate root ş-k-w "to complain".
Arabic root ḍ-m-m; zam (addition), zamime (supplement), zammetmek, munzam (added), zamlı and zamlanmak come from the same root. Zem and zimmet belong to the separate root ḏ-m-m.
Arabic root ʿ-d-n; maʿdin "mine, source" > maden, madeni, madenci, madencilik and madenbilim come from the same root. Medeniyet belongs to the separate root m-d-n "to become urbanized".

Arabic root w-ḍ-ʿ; vaz (placing), vazetmek, mevzu (what is placed; topic), mevzuat, mevzi, vaziyet, tevazu (humility) and mütevazi come from the same root. Veda and mevduat belong to the separate root w-d-ʿ "to entrust".
Arabic root f-y-ḍ; fayḍ (overflow, abundance) > feyiz, feyyaz and feyezan (flood) derive from the same root. Fayda and istifade belong to the separate root f-y-d "to be of use".
Arabic root ġ-n-y; ġannā "to sing" > muganni (singer) and teganni (singing) come from this root. Nağme is a separate word from the root n-ġ-m "melody".
Arabic root r-ʾ-y; ruʾyā (seeing; dream) > rüya, riyāʾ (ostentation) > riya and murāʾī (hypocrite) > mürai come from the same root. Mera and riayet belong to the separate root r-ʿ-y "to tend".
Arabic root c-d-l; mucādala (contention, struggle) > mücadele and mücadeleci come from the same root. Cihat and mücahit belong to the separate root c-h-d "to strive".
Latin flectere "to bend, to turn" (past participle flexus); refleks (bent back; an automatic response), fleksiyon (bending), fleksibl (flexible) and refleksif derive from the same root.

ʿanʿana, built by repeating the Arabic preposition ʿan "from", names the chain of transmission of a hadith ("from so-and-so, who had it from so-and-so"); from there anane (an'ane) came to mean "tradition handed down from generation to generation", and ananevi (traditional) shares the root.
